throughout the night, I sought him whom my soul loves.
I sought him, and did not find him.
and I will circle through the city.
Through the side streets and thoroughfares,
et plateas quæram quem diligit anima mea:
I will seek him whom my soul loves.
Invenerunt me vigiles qui custodiunt civitatem:
The watchers who guard the city found me:
Num quem diligit anima mea vidistis?
“Have you seen him whom my soul loves?”
When I had passed by them a little,
I found him whom my soul loves.
donec introducam illum in domum matris meæ,
until I would bring him into my mother’s house,
and into the chamber of her who bore me.
by the does and the stags of the open field,
not to disturb or awaken the beloved,
Quæ est ista quæ ascendit per desertum sicut virgula fumi ex aromatibus myrrhæ, et thuris, et universi pulveris pigmentarii?
Chorus to Groom: Who is she, who ascends through the desert, like a staff of smoke from the aromatics of myrrh, and frankincense, and every powder of the perfumer?
En lectulum Salomonis sexaginta fortes ambiunt ex fortissimis Israël,
Chorus to Bride: Lo, sixty strong ones, out of all the strongest in Israel, stand watch at the bed of Solomon,
all holding swords and well-trained in warfare,
each one’s weapon upon his thigh,
uniuscujusque ensis super femur suum propter timores nocturnos.
because of fears in the night.
Ferculum fecit sibi rex Salomon de lignis Libani;
Bride to Chorus: King Solomon made himself a portable throne from the wood of Lebanon.
He made its columns of silver,
out of charity for the daughters of Jerusalem.
go forth and see king Solomon with the diadem with which his mother crowned him,
regem Salomonem in diademate quo coronavit illum mater sua in die desponsationis illius,
on the day of his espousal,
et in die lætitiæ cordis ejus.
on the day of the rejoicing of his heart.
